expert_background: CIO and SVP at Wawa, Inc. ($20B convenience retailer, 990+ locations, 43,000 associates; IT org ~650, about half outsourced); previously CIO at TracFone and Global Chief Technology Architect at Walmart
summary: Expert background: CIO and SVP at Wawa ($20B convenience retail, 990+ stores), running a ~650-person IT org with about half outsourced, first-level support offshore. He estimates at least 30% to 50% of ITSM work can be done by agents or AI today and says only about 20% of IT issues are ever logged as tickets, so proactive agent monitoring could address the unlogged 80%. He calls ServiceNow the 'Cadillac' of ITSM but very expensive, says Now Assist does not really do the job, and is testing ServiceNow plus Moveworks, budgeting add-on AI at about 20% of the core ITSM cost. He questions whether he will need ServiceNow at all, describing it as 'just a bunch of data' that agents could replace, and prefers a multi-vendor approach over one platform. He frames the future as outcome-based agents that 'repair, replace, do whatever' to achieve a stated outcome within three to five years.
